doc: Field camera director defaults (M1-ARC-01, docs/kb/tech/field_camera.md). A CameraShot overrides any of these; negative / empty in a shot means 'use the default here'.

eases.doc: Named blend curves: Tween transition + ease, sampled with Tween.interpolate_value.

keep_in_frame_doc: PAN_FOLLOW keeps the leader within keep_in_frame_share of the frame's half angles of its aim, vertically (the shot's fov) and horizontally (from keep_in_frame_aspect, the 1920 x 1080 reference): when a shot's capped pan (max_pan_deg) would lose him, the aim turns just enough to hold him; a composition with him on a third stays as authored (FieldCameraDirector.keep_in_frame; the Lead's 10-29 walk audit).

orbit.doc: Only when the director's hub_orbit_enabled flag is set (SPEC §6.6: no free orbit except optional hub zones).

follow.doc: CameraShot.Mode.FOLLOW defaults (ADR 0194): metres back from the player along the shot's heading, and up.

occlusion.doc: The PC's real-GPU Act I QA (row 38, Coilspire): a wall the player sees standing between a volume shot's camera and the leader's chest (chest_m over his feet) pulls the camera in along that line to margin_m short of it, at once; with the view clear it eases back out at release_mps. Never nearer the leader than min_distance_m. A wall is a drawn mesh, tested by its triangles (collision misses walls and has walls nobody sees): every MeshInstance3D at least min_size_m across with no transparent surface, the leader's own body aside; hidden meshes don't count. Scripted (cutscene) shots are composed and left alone.
